Remote and Work-From-Home Jobs in the U.S.: Full-Time, Part-Time, and Where to Apply

By The Jobs World Editorial Team · Updated September 2026

Remote and work-from-home jobs are more common than ever — in customer service, data entry, virtual assistance, tutoring and content review. This free guide covers the roles hiring most often in the United States, the part-time and flexible work that fits around a family, and the reputable boards and employers to apply through. Applying from outside the U.S.? Start with our international guide.

Popular types of remote jobs

These are the roles hiring most often, with the pay ranges commonly advertised. Actual pay is set by each employer and shown on the official posting.

Customer Service Rep$15 – $22 / hr Data Entry Clerk$15 – $20 / hr Virtual Assistant$16 – $25 / hr Remote Sales / Appointment Setter$17 – $28 / hr Content Moderator / QA$16 – $23 / hr

Part-time and flexible work that fits around your day

If you need work that bends around school hours, caring for someone at home, or another job, these are the options that genuinely flex. Most are paid per task, per lesson or per audio minute rather than by a fixed shift — which is what makes the hours yours, and also why the income moves week to week.

  • Customer support, part-time Contact-centre employers regularly post 15–25 hour schedules, including evenings and weekends. Paid hourly, and training is usually provided.
  • Online tutoring and language practice Teach a school subject or practise conversation by video. Usually paid per lesson, with students booking into hours you open yourself.
  • Data annotation and search evaluation Rate search results, label images, or check AI answers against written guidelines. Task-based, so you work when you are free.
  • Transcription and captioning Type what you hear from short audio or video files. Paid per audio minute, so the hours are entirely your own.
  • Virtual assistant, a few hours a day Inbox, calendar and small admin tasks for one client. Once you have a regular client this is the steadiest of the flexible options.
  • Paid research studies and website tests Short paid studies and usability tests. Genuinely flexible, but treat it as supplemental income — the work arrives irregularly and it is not a job.

Where to find flexible, part-time work

Platforms that recruit for the flexible roles above. Most of them hire in many countries, so this list is worth checking wherever you are based. Each opens on the platform's own site, and all of them are free to join.

  • Appen Task-based work-from-home projects — data annotation, search evaluation — recruited across a long list of countries. Projects come and go, so check back.
  • TELUS Digital Recruits part-time, from-home raters and data contributors internationally. Each project lists the countries and languages it needs.
  • Clickworker Short micro-tasks paid per task — text, categorisation, data checks. Open in many countries; how much is available changes week to week.
  • Preply Tutor a subject or a language online. You set your own rate and open only the hours you actually want to teach.
  • italki Teach a language by video call to students worldwide, entirely on a schedule you control.
  • TranscribeMe Transcribe short audio files from home once you pass their entry test. Paid per audio minute, worked whenever suits you.

Applying from outside the United States?

Most of the U.S. listings above will not take an application from abroad — the employer has to run payroll and tax in the country you live in, so their postings stay inside the states they already operate in. That is a legal and accounting limit, not a judgement about you, and there are routes that work around it.

Our international guide covers them: the boards that show which countries a company can hire in, the freelance platforms that connect you to clients abroad, the employers who genuinely hire across borders, and the job scams that target people applying from overseas.

Remote jobs from any country

How to spot and avoid remote-job scams

  • A legitimate employer never asks you to pay for a job, equipment or 'training' up front.
  • Apply on the company's own careers page or a reputable job board — not a link from a random text or DM.
  • Be wary of offers with no interview, instant hiring, or pay that sounds too good to be true.
  • Never share bank details or your SSN before you have a signed, verified offer.
  • Treat 'jobs' that arrive by WhatsApp or Telegram offering daily payments for simple tasks as a scam — that pattern is a task fraud, not employment.

Common questions

Are remote jobs legitimate?

Yes — many established companies hire remote customer service, data entry, tutoring and admin staff. The key is applying through official sites and reputable boards, which is what this guide links to.

What kind of remote work fits around school hours or family?

Work paid per task or per lesson rather than by a fixed shift: tutoring, transcription, data annotation and part-time virtual assistant work. Part-time customer service is the exception — it is hourly, but many employers post short evening and weekend schedules.

Can I get a U.S. remote job if I live in another country?

Sometimes, but usually not as an employee — most U.S. postings are limited to the U.S. because the employer has to run payroll and tax where you live. The routes that do work are covered in our guide to remote jobs you can do from any country, linked above.

How much can I earn working part-time from home?

It varies too much to promise a figure. Task-based work pays per item completed and the volume changes week to week. Each platform publishes its own rates and the official posting is the only reliable source — treat any site that guarantees you a specific daily income as a warning sign.

Do I need experience or a degree to work from home?

Often not. Customer service, data entry, annotation and transcription usually test you rather than ask for a CV, and training is common. Tutoring and freelance work depend on demonstrable skill rather than formal qualifications.

What equipment do I need?

Usually a reliable computer and internet connection, and a quiet space for calls. Some employers provide equipment — the posting will say. You should never have to buy equipment from the employer itself.

How do I avoid work-from-home scams?

A real job never asks you to pay to start. Apply only through the official links above, and never send money or bank details before a verified offer.
